To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Arabidopsis encodes a bacterial-like heterodimeric 2-malyl-CoA:pyruvate carboxyltransferase involved in both Leucine biosynthesis and the Methionine chain elongation pathway for glucosinolide formation.

the isopropyl malate isomerase of Arabidopsis thalanica is a heterodimeric enzyme composed of two different subunits, and that these two subunits are involved in the isomerisation of the 2-malates in both the leucine biosynthetic pathway, and the chain elongation cycle of glucosinolite biosynthesis.
the isomerization of 2-malates to 3-malates in Arabidopsis is catalyzed by two different heterotetrameric isopropyl malate isomerases, each composed of one large subunit and two small subunits.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a novel mechanism for the control of the flux of carbon through two pathways in a plant, the Leu biosynthesis pathway and the Met elongation cycle of glucosinolase biosynthesis, which are linked at the level of isomerization of 2-malates to 3-malates.

the analysis of the genes encoding the second step of a reaction sequence that is common to the biosynthetic pathway of Leu and the Met chain-elongation pathway of glucinolates, the two most prominent amino acids of the Brassicaceae.
the characterization of the genes encoding the second reaction type of the last steps of the Met chain and the Leu biosynthesis pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IPMI small and large subunits have different functions and are localized in different compartments of the cell.
the IPMI small chain subunits determine the substrate specificity of the IPMI large chain subunit.
the IPMI large subunit has a function in both pathways, whereas the small subunits are specialized in one or the other pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the isomerization step of the common pathway for Leu biosynthesis in the cytosol and the Met chain extension cycle in the plastid is performed by two different heterodimerized IPMI enzymes.

the isomerization step in Leu biosynthesis is catalyzed by a chloroplast localized heterodimeric bacterial-type IPMI, while a cytosolic homodimeric IPMI is responsible for isomerization reactions of the Met chain-elongation pathway in glucosinolate biosynthesis.
the Leu and glucosinolate biosynthetic pathways are evolutionarily related and that the chloroplast is the site of glucosinolite biosynthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the isomerization step in the Met chain elongating cycle is catalyzed by the same enzyme that isomerizes isopropyl-malate in the Leu biosynthesis pathway.
the isomerization reactions in both pathways are catalyzed by the same enzyme, and that the small subunit determines the substrate specificity of the enzyme.
the isomerization step is the rate-limiting reaction of the Leu and the glucosinolate pathways.
